title: The kernel of n ↦ n mod 5
caption: The homomorphism φ(n) = n mod 5 sends the multiples of 5 (the kernel 5ℤ) to 0. Every other value has its own fibre, a copy of the kernel shifted along: the integers sent to 3 are …, −7, −2, 3, 8, ….
alt: A number line from −10 to 10. The multiples of 5 are marked as the kernel and the integers −7, −2, 3 and 8, which all map to 3, are marked as a second set, each five apart.
description: The line shows the integers from −10 to 10.
The kernel, the integers that φ sends to 0, is the multiples of 5: −10, −5, 0, 5, 10.
The integers that φ sends to 3 are −7, −2, 3, 8: the kernel shifted by 3.
Each fibre is a coset of the kernel, so ℤ/5ℤ has five elements and is isomorphic to ℤ₅.

checks.name: -10 is a multiple of 5, so φ(-10) = 0
-5 is a multiple of 5, so φ(-5) = 0
0 is a multiple of 5, so φ(0) = 0
5 is a multiple of 5, so φ(5) = 0
10 is a multiple of 5, so φ(10) = 0
-7 − 3 is a multiple of 5, so φ(-7) = 3
-2 − 3 is a multiple of 5, so φ(-2) = 3
3 − 3 is a multiple of 5, so φ(3) = 3
8 − 3 is a multiple of 5, so φ(8) = 3
